text:
sophia: quick sync 1 want alignment on the 'route governance launch canvas' for long-term platform routing. goal: agree gating and migration runway for multi-region + per-tenant isolation. asking for decisions by EOD Friday.

kai: can you list the concrete gates? ill validate SLO and infra impact quickly. :clock1:

sophia: proposed gates (draft):
- pilot: onboard 2-3 pilot customers onto isolated slices for 14 days
- resilience: cross-region failover run with <5% error budget burn in canary stage
- economics: per-tenant unit cost delta must be <= 15% or have compensating pricing
- security/compliance: KMS + audit trail enabled on private/deployed lanes
- quality: canonical prompt regression <= 3% measured on eval harness

aleks: +1 on pilots. request: add a soft-throttle quarantine before hard-eviction for noisy tenants. also we need to define what counts as a "compatible variant" (e.g., 8-bit quantized vs full fp16) and document expected semantic shift.

jordan: we must decide on runbook ownership for reroutes. ops currently owns infra, CS owns customer comms. proposal: ops lead incident, CS owns customer rollback/communication.

kai: infra metrics to gate on: p50/p95 latency per model family, request success rate, cold-standby spin-up; rough numbers to start: p95 < 350ms small, <650ms large; spin-up < 90s. i'll run capacity math when gates are final.

sophia: draft policy sketch for feedback (not final):
```yaml
policy_name: governance_canvas_v1
priority_order:
  - local_region
  - compatible_variant
  - regional_peers
  - cold_standby
max_total_latency_ms: 1200
tenant_controls:
  pin_to_region: optional
  burst_window_sec: 120
  quarantine_threshold_error_frac: 0.2
```

aleks: suggest switching quarantine_threshold to absolute error counts + anomaly pattern check, fractional thresholds can misfire for tiny tenants.

jordan: on "compatible_variant": do we permit automatic model downgrades that may alter semantics? customers should explicitly opt in. add a quality-monitoring rollback and explicit consent flag.

sophia: agreed 1 gate will mandate a pre-approved opt-in path with automatic regression checks; fail gate if regression > 3%.

kai: migration runway proposed: sandbox -> shadowing (mirrored traffic) -> staged cutover with validation window. per-tenant timeline estimate: 48-72h plus automated validations. warm-standby option if customer pays for reserved capacity.

aleks: note: Sales asked about "burst credits" (paid temporary capacity). add as commercial lever; requires throttles and billing hooks.

infra-bot: created INFRA-5247 (https://go/redwood/infra/INFRA-5247). actions: add chaos tests, update canary pipeline, add slice-level metrics dashboard.

sophia: decisions we need before we draft the launch canvas doc:
1) endorse final gate list (pilot/resilience/econ/security/quality)
2) define compatible-variant semantics and opt-in UX
3) approve migration runway template and cost model for warm standbys
4) confirm runbook ownership and communication flow for reroutes

kai: i'll own SLO validation and infra test definitions (1 & 3).

aleks: i'll draft the opt-in UX and quality rollback flow (2).

jordan: i'll produce a runbook ownership proposal and loop in support (4).

sophia: good. i'll assemble the canvas doc and circulate to PMs + sales for pilot candidates. next check-in Tuesday 09:30 PT.

aleks: small ask: can we include a "graceful throttling" mode with a refund/credit policy? might make pilots easier to sell.

kai: technically feasible, but needs billing integration and throttling enforcement. cost attribution may be noisy.

sophia: adding both "burst credits" and "graceful throttling with credits" as optional commercial levers in canvas.

infra-bot: reminder: canary window scheduled Mon 03/30 00:00 UTC.

sophia: thanks everyone 1 i'll post the canvas link when updated. closing thread.
